title: The Trees and the Axe
text:
A man walked into a forest carrying an axe head with no handle. He went to the trees and asked them politely for a piece of wood to make one. It seemed a small request, and the great trees talked it over and agreed. They chose a young ash tree, one of the least important among them, and gave it to him.

The man shaped the ash into a strong handle and fitted it to his axe. Then he set to work. He did not stop at a sapling or two. Stroke after stroke, he cut down the oldest and noblest trees of the forest, the giants that had stood there for centuries.

As the man moved through the wood, an old oak watched its companions fall. It turned to a cedar standing nearby and said that their first step had ruined them all. If they had stood up for the ash, they might all have stood for ages. By handing over the weakest of their number, they had given the enemy the very tool that brought them down.
lesson: Do not sacrifice a weaker member of your group to buy peace. What you hand over to an opponent can become the tool used against everyone.
source: Aesop's Fables, The Trees and the Axe
